newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU prepares for hasty meeting with Arafat.
newsitem.headline: EU prepares for hasty meeting with Arafat.

text.p: The European Union moved to restore lost influence in the Middle East peace process on Monday with a hastily-arranged meeting of some of its foreign ministers with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

Arafat was due in Luxembourg on Monday evening for talks with the EU's "troika", made up of the foreign ministers of the 15-nation bloc's past, current and future presidents, in this case Italy, Ireland and the Netherlands.
Some EU countries -- notably France -- are angered at being left out of a summit called by U.S. President Bill Clinton for Washington this week.
Apart from Clinton and Arafat, the Washington summit will be attended by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.

The snub has irritated some European governments, who are the main paymasters of the U.S.-dominated peace process but have been denied a high-profile political role ever since the 1991 Madrid peace conference which launched it.
French Foreign Ministry Herve de Charette vented frustration in a radio interview on Sunday at Europe's exclusion from the Washington summit.
"That is certainly unfortunate," he said. "That is certainly not a positive step for things to go forward."
But not everyone shared French pique. British officials said Washington had co-ordinated closely with the Europeans, even if the EU was not at the table.
"We welcome the prospect of the summit. It seems perfectly sensible that it should be held under the auspices of the United States," a British foreign office spokesman told Reuters.
Another EU diplomat said on Monday that the snub to the EU -- whether intended or not -- was unimportant as long as the Washington summit helped restore peace.

He said the idea to invite Arafat to address a regular meeting of EU foreign ministers on Tuesday had been discussed as early as last Friday, after a wave of violence sparked by the opening of an Israeli tunnel in the Arab Old City of Jerusalem.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said the meeting was being held "at the express request of Italy".

"Tonight's meeting of the European troika with President (Yasser) Arafat in Luxembourg...underlines the role of Europe in the Middle East peace process, especially since it is being held before the Washington summit," he told Reuters in Rome.
Diplomats said the troika would pledge continued financial and other aid to the fledgling Palestinian state, but would also be urging Arafat to do all he could to reduce tension in the Middle east.
Arafat was due to meet the troika over dinner, after which he would also hold bilateral talks with Dini.

A French foreign ministry spokesman said Arafat would meet De Charette on Tuesday morning before continuing on to Washington. But a spokesman for Ireland -- the current EU president -- said details of Arafat's itinerary could not be finalised until after he had met with the troika.

Diplomats said Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak had sought to include France or the EU's Irish presidency in the summit line-up but had met with a flat refusal from the United States and Israel.
The three major EU powers, France, Britain and Germany, made an unprecedented joint appeal to Netanyahu and Arafat last Friday to resume top-level peace negotiations immediately.
Unlike the United States, which has refrained from public criticism of the Jewish state, they called for the closure of the Israeli tunnel which triggered last week's violence.

It was the first such joint foreign policy initiative by the "Big Three", and was aimed at maximising European influence and responding to complaints that the EU was too slow and powerless in reacting to crises close to its borders.
